Subject: Private deployment - EU/APAC custody handshake and standby routing

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the call earlier today. Indigo is moving forward with a Private deployment scoped to EU production + APAC warm-standby. Before procurement signs off we need a written confirmation of the following items so our legal and security teams can close the residency checklist: 

- Which cluster(s) hold customer data at rest (EU primary vs APAC standby) and precise storage boundaries.
- The failover trigger criteria (automatic vs manual) and estimated RTO/RPO for an APAC->EU or EU->APAC switch.
- Network egress patterns during failover (will data transit third-party regions?).
- Evidence artifacts (logs, audit proof) you can provide to demonstrate a non-transit guarantee for EU production data except in deliberate failover scenarios.

We appreciate a short delta doc and any diagrams. Procurement also needs a simple acceptance checklist we can attach to the PO.

Best,
Sara

Sara — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together the short answers below and attached a diagram and an evidence bundle for your team to review. Happy to run through this on a 30-min call if you prefer.

Short answers:
- Data at rest location: EU primary cluster (Frankfurt region) holds all production customer data for Indigo APAC production tenant. APAC warm-standby (Singapore) holds encrypted KV cache + warmed model weights only; no persistent customer PII or transaction records are written to APAC disks under normal operation.
- Failover triggers: automated health-based detection with operator confirmation by default. We support a forced automatic failover in emergency but require pre-agreed conditions — by default RTO (operator-driven) ~ 20 minutes, RPO < 5 minutes (KV-cache replay). For automatic emergency failover RTO ~ 5–10 minutes with higher reconciliation steps.
- Egress during failover: during controlled failover we replicate minimal metadata and checkpoint KV blobs via our secure peering channels between EU and APAC. All replication uses TLS 1.3 over private VPC peering; we do not route through third-party transit regions.
- Evidence: attached is a residency-evidence-pack containing control-plane audit logs, KMS key IDs scoped to the EU keyring, and a network topology diagram showing private peering flows.

Deliverables attached: redwood-private-deploy-standby-routing-diagram.pdf, residency-evidence-pack.zip.

Next steps / acceptance checklist (suggested):
1) Indigo infra confirms the acceptance checklist fields below.
2) We schedule a 60-minute tabletop to walk the handover and run a simulation.
3) On acceptance we will produce a signed deployment attestation and provide the artifacts for the procurement PO.

Proposed acceptance checklist (we will format into a one-page doc):
- Primary cluster and partition IDs documented
- KMS key IDs and rotation policy confirmed
- Failover playbook and operator contact list confirmed
- Network peering circuits and advertised prefixes approved
- Test window scheduled for a failover drill

If you want me to drop this into a one-pager for procurement, I can do that and include a short runbook excerpt.

Ben

Hi Sara, Ben — adding a few compliance clarifications from Product/Private Deploy: 

- Storage topology: EU disks are mounted to the Frankfurt tenant nodes; snapshots are retained in the EU region S3 bucket with IAM policies that deny replication to other regions except during the explicit cross-region transfer job (which is used only for DR exercises and requires operator approval and DocuSign confirmation).
- KMS scope: KMS keys are customer-scoped and can be restricted to the EU keyring. We will provide key ARNs and a sample key policy for your security team to vet.
- Auditability: We will provide a signed digest (SHA256) of the retention logs and a time-limited signed URL to the audit bundle in Drive. That bundle contains control-plane events mapping to the storage lifecycle.

I'll put together the one-pager and a canonical acceptance checklist you can attach to the PO. Ben — we'll need a copy of Indigo's approved operator list and a primary emergency contact for the tabletop.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Product Manager, Redwood Private Deploy

Sara — quick answers inline and next steps: 

1) Transient storage: explicit confirmation — PII and transaction payloads are not written to APAC disks under any failover mode. During emergency failover, metadata and checkpoint blobs necessary for state reconstruction may traverse the private peering link but are buffered in encrypted transit and only written to the warm-standby's ephemeral cache which is configured with a strict TTL and auto-sanitization post-reconciliation. We will provide a technical note describing the buffer flow and retention TTL.

2) DocuSign operator-confirmation: attached a sample operator-confirmation template and an example DocuSign envelope ID. The template requires two operator signatures and one Indigo authorization stamp before a forced automatic failover is executed.

3) Tabletop slots: Tuesday 2028-01-17 09:00–10:00 UTC or Wednesday 2028-01-18 14:00–15:00 UTC. Please confirm which works for your team.

Indemnity statement: Redwood will include a limited indemnity clause tied to documented misconfiguration by Redwood's operational team. We cannot accept broad cross-border indemnity for customer-initiated configuration changes; we will share proposed contractual language and are open to redlines through your legal team.
